TJS2 VM

　TJS2 compiles scripts into binary code for a virtual machine (TJS2 VM) before executing them.
　Since the disassembled result of this TJS2 VM code is displayed when an exception occurs or when a dump is performed, this section briefly explains this virtual machine.

Instruction Codes

　The TJS2 VM is independent for each execution unit such as functions and properties, and a single function never shares instruction code space, register space, flags, or constant area with other functions.
　The instruction pointer (ip) always starts at 0 at the beginning of a function, etc.
　An instruction code represented by a simple human-readable name is called a mnemonic.

Registers

　Registers in the TJS2 VM are represented as %(number) in mnemonics. The number can also be negative. There is no limit on the number of registers. Local variables and temporary values during calculation are all stored in registers. Main memory and stacks do not exist.
　The values represented by registers are the same as TJS2 variables, and can represent integers, real numbers, objects, strings, octet streams, and void.
　In the current version, register %0 is always void. Register %-1 is 'this'. Register %-2 is a special object called this proxy; when member access is performed on this object, it first checks 'this', and if not found there, it checks 'global'. The 'this proxy' does not exist in global-level execution units. Arguments to functions, etc. are stored in advance in registers such as %-3 and %-4 when execution begins.
　Values of registers other than those with predetermined uses or pre-filled values like these are undefined at the start of execution.

Flags

　The TJS2 VM has only one flag, which stores comparison results. The flag takes only true or false values.

Constant Area

　The constant area of the TJS2 VM is a location where constants are stored, represented as *(number) in mnemonics. The constant area is read-only, and the const instruction is used to transfer values from this constant area to registers. In addition, "names" used to access object members by name, such as function names and property names, are also stored in this constant area.

VM Mnemonic List

　Some operands take forms such as %obj.*name or %obj.%name, which involve referencing object members.
　Operands in the form %obj.*name perform direct references, accessing a member with the name represented by *name from the object represented by register %obj.
　Operands in the form %obj.%name perform indirect references, accessing a member with the name represented by %name from the object represented by register %obj.
　Mnemonics for such instructions have suffixes d or pd (direct / property direct) or i or pi (indirect / property indirect).
　Instructions with a suffix containing p invoke the property handler of the target register (performing the operation of the unary '*' operator).


nop
(no operation)
　Does nothing.
const
(copy constant value)
Format: const %dest, *src

　Copies the value of the constant area specified by *src to the register specified by %dest.
cp
(copy register)
Format: cp %dest, %src

　Copies the value of the register specified by %src to the register specified by %dest.
cl
(clear register)
Format: cl %dest

　Sets the register specified by %dest to void.
ccl
(clear register)
Format: ccl %low-%high

　Sets all registers in the range from %low to %high to void.
tt
(test true)
Format: tt %reg

　Sets the flag to true if the register specified by %reg represents true, or false if it represents false.
tf
(test false)
Format: tf %reg

　Opposite of tt; sets the flag to false if the register specified by %reg represents true, or true if it represents false.
ceq
(compare equal)
Format: ceq %reg1, %reg2

　Sets the flag to true if %reg1 and %reg2 match in standard comparison (behavior of == operator), otherwise false.
cdeq
(compare distinct equal)
Format: cdeq %reg1, %reg2

　Sets the flag to true if %reg1 and %reg2 match in identity comparison (behavior of === operator), otherwise false.
clt
(compare littler than)
Format: clt %reg1, %reg2

　Sets the flag to true if %reg1 > %reg2, otherwise false.
cgt
(compare greater than)
Format: cgt %reg1, %reg2

　Sets the flag to true if %reg1 < %reg2, otherwise false.
setf
(set flag)
Format: setf %dest

　If the flag is true, sets %dest to true (non-zero integer); if false, sets to false (integer 0).
setnf
(set not flag)
Format: setnf %dest

　Opposite of setf; if the flag is false, sets %dest to true (non-zero integer); if true, sets to false (integer 0).
lnot
(logical not)
Format: lnot %reg

　Inverts the truth value of %reg.
nf
(not flag)
Format: nf

　Inverts the truth value of the flag.
jf
(jump if flag)
Format: jf ip

　Jumps to ip if the flag is true.
jnf
(jump if not flag)
Format: jnf ip

　Jumps to ip if the flag is false.
inc, incpd, incpi, incp
(increment)
Format: inc %reg
Format: incpd %res, %obj.*name
Format: incpi %res, %obj.%name
Format: incp %res, %propobj

　Increments %reg, %obj.*name, %obj.%name, or %propobj.
　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
dec, decpd, decpi, decp
(decrement)
Format: dec %reg
Format: decpd %res, %obj.*name
Format: decpi %res, %obj.%name
Format: decp %res, %propobj

　Decrements %reg, %obj.*name, %obj.%name, or %propobj.
　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
lor, lorpd, lorpi, lorp
(logical or)
Format: lor %dest, %src

　Performs logical OR on %dest and %src, and stores the result in %dest.

Format: lorpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Performs logical OR on %obj.*name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name.

Format: lorpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Performs logical OR on %obj.%name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name.

Format: lorp %res, %propobj, %src

　Performs logical OR on %propobj and %src, and stores the result in %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
land, landpd, landpi, landp
(logical and)
Format: land %dest, %src

　Performs logical AND on %dest and %src, and stores the result in %dest.

Format: landpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Performs logical AND on %obj.*name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name.

Format: landpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Performs logical AND on %obj.%name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name.

Format: landp %res, %propobj, %src

　Performs logical AND on %propobj and %src, and stores the result in %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
bor, borpd, borpi, borp
(bitwise or)
Format: bor %dest, %src

　Performs bitwise OR on %dest and %src, and stores the result in %dest.

Format: borpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Performs bitwise OR on %obj.*name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name.

Format: borpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Performs bitwise OR on %obj.%name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name.

Format: borp %res, %propobj, %src

　Performs bitwise OR on %propobj and %src, and stores the result in %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
bxor, bxorpd, bxorpi, bxorp
(bitwise xor)
Format: bxor %dest, %src

　Performs bitwise XOR on %dest and %src, and stores the result in %dest.

Format: bxorpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Performs bitwise XOR on %obj.*name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name.

Format: bxorpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Performs bitwise XOR on %obj.%name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name.

Format: bxorp %res, %propobj, %src

　Performs bitwise XOR on %propobj and %src, and stores the result in %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
band, bandpd, bandpi, bandp
(bitwise and)
Format: band %dest, %src

　Performs bitwise AND on %dest and %src, and stores the result in %dest.

Format: bandpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Performs bitwise AND on %obj.*name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name.

Format: bandpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Performs bitwise AND on %obj.%name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name.

Format: bandp %res, %propobj, %src

　Performs bitwise AND on %propobj and %src, and stores the result in %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
sar, sarpd, sarpi, sarp
(shift arithmetic right)
Format: sar %dest, %src

　Shifts %dest arithmetically to the right by the count specified by %src, and stores the result in %dest.

Format: sarpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Shifts %obj.*name arithmetically to the right by the count specified by %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name.

Format: sarpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Shifts %obj.%name arithmetically to the right by the count specified by %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name.

Format: sarp %res, %propobj, %src

　Shifts %propobj arithmetically to the right by the count specified by %src, and stores the result in %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
sal, salpd, salpi, salp
(shift arithmetic left)
Format: sal %dest, %src

　Shifts %dest arithmetically to the left by the count specified by %src, and stores the result in %dest.

Format: salpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Shifts %obj.*name arithmetically to the left by the count specified by %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name.

Format: salpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Shifts %obj.%name arithmetically to the left by the count specified by %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name.

Format: salp %res, %propobj, %src

　Shifts %propobj arithmetically to the left by the count specified by %src, and stores the result in %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
sr, srpd, srpi, srp
(shift bitwise right)
Format: sr %dest, %src

　Shifts %dest bitwise to the right by the count specified by %src, and stores the result in %dest.

Format: srpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Shifts %obj.*name bitwise to the right by the count specified by %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name.

Format: srpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Shifts %obj.%name bitwise to the right by the count specified by %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name.

Format: srp %res, %propobj, %src

　Shifts %propobj bitwise to the right by the count specified by %src, and stores the result in %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
add, addpd, addpi, addp
(add)
Format: add %dest, %src

　Adds %src to %dest, and stores the result in %dest.

Format: addpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Adds %src to %obj.*name, and stores the result in %obj.*name.

Format: addpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Adds %src to %obj.%name, and stores the result in %obj.%name.

Format: addp %res, %propobj, %src

　Adds %src to %propobj, and stores the result in %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
sub, subpd, subpi, subp
(subtract)
Format: sub %dest, %src

　Subtracts %src from %dest, and stores the result in %dest.

Format: subpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Subtracts %src from %obj.*name, and stores the result in %obj.*name.

Format: subpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Subtracts %src from %obj.%name, and stores the result in %obj.%name.

Format: subp %res, %propobj, %src

　Subtracts %src from %propobj, and stores the result in %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
mod, modpd, modpi, modp
(modulo)
Format: mod %dest, %src

　Stores the remainder of %dest divided by %src into %dest.

Format: modpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Stores the remainder of %obj.*name divided by %src into %obj.*name.

Format: modpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Stores the remainder of %obj.%name divided by %src into %obj.%name.

Format: modp %res, %propobj, %src

　Stores the remainder of %propobj divided by %src into %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
div, divpd, divpi, divp
(real divide)
Format: div %dest, %src

　Performs real division of %dest by %src, and stores the result in %dest.

Format: divpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Performs real division of %obj.*name by %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name.

Format: divpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Performs real division of %obj.%name by %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name.

Format: divp %res, %propobj, %src

　Performs real division of %propobj by %src, and stores the result in %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
idiv, idivpd, idivpi, idivp
(integer divide)
Format: idiv %dest, %src

　Performs integer division of %dest by %src, and stores the result in %dest.

Format: idivpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Performs integer division of %obj.*name by %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name.

Format: idivpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Performs integer division of %obj.%name by %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name.

Format: divp %res, %propobj, %src

　Performs integer division of %propobj by %src, and stores the result in %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
mul, mulpd, mulpi, mulp
(multiply)
Format: mul %dest, %src

　Multiplies %dest by %src, and stores the result in %dest.

Format: mulpd %res, %obj.*name, %src

　Multiplies %obj.*name by %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name.

Format: mulpi %res, %obj.%name, %src

　Multiplies %obj.%name by %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name.

Format: mulp %res, %propobj, %src

　Multiplies %propobj by %src, and stores the result in %propobj.

　Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
bnot
(bitwise not)
Format: bnot %reg

　Inverts the bitwise truth value of %reg and stores it back in %reg.
asc
(make ascii string)
Format: asc %reg

　Creates a single character corresponding to the numeric value represented by %reg and stores it back in %reg.
chr
(cheracter code)
Format: chr %reg

　Stores the character code of the first character of the string represented by %reg into %reg.
num
(number)
Format: num %reg

　Converts the register represented by %reg to a number.
chs
(change sign)
Format: chs %reg

　Inverts the sign of the numeric value of the register represented by %reg.
inv
(invalidate)
Format: inv %reg

　Invalidates the object represented by %reg.
chkinv
(invalidate)
Format: chkinv %reg

　Sets %reg to true if the object represented by %reg is not invalidated, otherwise false.
int
(convert to integer)
Format: int %reg

　Converts the register represented by %reg to an integer.
real
(convert to real)
Format: real %reg

　Converts the register represented by %reg to a real number.
string
(convert to string)
Format: string %reg

　Converts the register represented by %reg to a string.
octet
(convert to octet)
Format: octet %reg

　Converts the register represented by %reg to an octet stream.
typeof, typeofd, typeofi
(check type)
Format: typeof %reg
Format: typeofd %obj.*name
Format: typeofi %obj.%name

　Checks the type of %reg, %obj.*name, or %obj.%name, and stores the string representing that type back in %reg, %obj.*name, or %obj.%name.
eval
(evaluate expression)
Format: eval %reg

　Evaluates the string represented by %reg as an expression and stores the result back in %reg.
eexp
(execute expression)
Format: eexp %reg

　Executes the string represented by %reg as an expression and discards the result.
chkins
(check instance)
Format: chkins %reg, %classname

　Stores true in %reg if the object represented by %reg is an instance of the class whose name is represented by %classname, otherwise false.
call, calld, calli
(function call)
Format: call %dest, %func(%arg1, %arg2, %arg3, ...)
Format: calld %dest, %obj.*name(%arg1, %arg2, %arg3, ...)
Format: calli %dest, %obj.%name(%arg1, %arg2, %arg3, ...)

　Calls the function object represented by %func, %obj.*name, or %obj.%name with arguments %arg1, %arg2, %arg3 ..., and stores the result in %dest. If %dest is %0, the result is discarded (without being stored in %0).
new
(create new)
Format: new %dest, %func(%arg1, %arg2, %arg3, ...)

　Constructs the class object represented by %func with arguments %arg1, %arg2, %arg3 ..., and stores the result in %dest.
gpd, gpds
(get property direct)
Format: gpd %dest, %obj.*name
Format: gpds %dest, %obj.*name

　References the member represented by *name from the object represented by %obj and copies its value to %dest.
　gpd involves calling a property handler, whereas gpds does not call a property handler and gets the property object itself.
gpi, gpis
(get property indirect)
Format: gpi %dest, %obj.%name
Format: gpis %dest, %obj.%name

　References the member represented by %name from the object represented by %obj and copies its value to %dest.
　gpi involves calling a property handler, whereas gpis does not call a property handler and gets the property object itself.
spd, spde, spdeh, spds
(set property direct)
Format: spd %obj.*name
Format: spde %obj.*name
Format: spdeh %obj.*name
Format: spds %obj.*name

　Assigns the value of %src to the member represented by *name of the object represented by %obj.
　spd performs normal access, but throws an exception if the member does not exist.
　spde creates a new member if it does not exist.
　spdeh sets the member as a hidden member. It has no meaning in the current version.
　spds does not call a property handler and replaces the property object itself.
spi, spie, spis
(set property indirect)
Format: spi %obj.%name
Format: spie %obj.%name
Format: spis %obj.%name

　Assigns the value of %src to the member represented by %name of the object represented by %obj.
　spi performs normal access, but throws an exception if the member does not exist.
　spie creates a new member if it does not exist.
　spis does not call a property handler and replaces the property object itself.
getp
Format: getp %reg, %propobj

　Executes the getter of the property object represented by %propobj to obtain the property value, and assigns it to %reg. Performs the operation of the unary '*' operator.
setp
Format: setp %propobj, %reg

　Executes the setter of the property object represented by %propobj to set the value of %reg. Performs the operation of the unary '*' operator.
deld, deli
(delete member)
Format: deld %reg, %obj.*name
Format: deli %reg, %obj.%name

　Deletes the member represented by *name or %name of the object represented by %obj.
　Stores a boolean value indicating whether the deletion succeeded into %reg, but discards the result if %reg is %0.
srv
(set result value)
Format: srv %reg

　Sets the value of %reg as the return value of the function (the return value of the function becomes the value represented by %reg).
ret
(return)
Format: ret

　Returns to the caller.
entry
(enter try block)
Format: entry ip, %reg

　Enters an exception-protected block. If an exception occurs, jumps to ip and sets the exception object in %reg.
extry
(exit from try block)
Format: extry

　Exits from an exception-protected block.
throw
(throw exception object)
Format: throw %reg

　Throws the object represented by %reg as an exception object.
chgthis
(change this)
Format: chgthis %dest, %src

　Changes the closure part of the object represented by %dest to the object specified by %src.
global
(get global object)
Format: global %dest

　Stores the global object in %dest.
addci
(add class instance information)
Format: addci %dest, %info

　Adds %info to the class instance information of the object represented by %dest.
regmember
(register members)
Format: regmember

　Registers class members to the "this" object. Used internally.
debugger
(call debugger)
Format: debugger

　Suspends execution and calls the debugger. In the current version implementation, calls a native debugger instead of the TJS2 debugger.
